title: A Precise Measurement of the Fermi-LAT Galactic Center Excess Morphology and Spectrum
comment: 18 pages and 10 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: We present a new Fermi-LAT analysis of the Galactic-center excess (GCE) designed to substantially reduce the dominant systematic uncertainties associated with interstellar-emission and source modeling in the inner Galaxy. Using an optimized multi-step fitting procedure together with an iterative source-finding pipeline, we achieve a markedly improved agreement between data and model, reducing fractional residuals to $\lesssim 10\%$ over a $40^\circ\times 40^\circ$ region centered on the Galactic center. We analyze a suite of GALPROP-based interstellar-emission models (IEMs) and complementary analysis variants (Galactic-plane masking, fits restricted to $1$-$10$ GeV, and weighted-likelihood fits) to quantify robustness. The reconstructed surface-brightness profile is strongly centrally concentrated and is well described by an approximately spherical generalized Navarro-Frenk-White morphology with inner slope $γ\simeq 1.15$. Bulge-tracing templates (nuclear bulge plus boxy bulge) fail to reproduce the full radial morphology, most notably for line-of-sight angles around $θ\simeq 1^\circ$-$2^\circ$ and at $θ\gtrsim 8^\circ$, whereas the DM-motivated component provides a good description over the full angular range. Moreover, the DM component remains highly significant across all IEMs and analysis choices, including fits that simultaneously include the bulge templates. We also provide an updated measurement of the GCE spectrum from $0.5$ to $1000$ GeV, confirming a peak at a few GeV and setting stringent constraints above tens of GeV, where we obtain only upper limits at the level $E^2Φ\lesssim 10^{-8}$ GeV cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$. These results deliver a sharpened and systematically controlled characterization of the GCE morphology and spectrum, enabling more incisive tests of astrophysical and dark-matter interpretations.

AI.tldr: This work presents an improved Fermi-LAT analysis of the Galactic-center excess with reduced systematic uncertainties, demonstrating a highly significant dark matter-like component well-fitted by a Navarro-Frenk-White profile, and confirming the GCE spectral shape with stringent constraints at high energies.
AI.motivation: To reduce dominant systematic uncertainties in the analysis of the Galactic-center excess (GCE) related to interstellar-emission and source modeling.
AI.method: A new Fermi-LAT analysis employing an optimized multi-step fitting procedure combined with an iterative source-finding pipeline, analysis of various interstellar-emission models, and complementary analysis variants including Galactic-plane masking and weighted-likelihood fits.
AI.result: Achieved improved data-model agreement with fractional residuals below 10% over a 40°x40° region, reconstructed a strongly centrally concentrated GCE surface-brightness profile matching a spherical generalized Navarro-Frenk-White morphology with inner slope γ≈1.15, found the DM-motivated component provides a better fit than bulge-tracing templates, and confirmed a GCE spectral peak at a few GeV with stringent upper limits above tens of GeV.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a refined and systematically controlled characterization of the GCE morphology and spectrum, strengthening the support for a dark matter component across all models and analysis methods, and enabling improved tests of astrophysical versus dark matter origins.

title: Strong X-ray Variability of I Zwicky 1: Obscuration from Clumpy Accretion-Disk Winds
comment: 24 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: Obscuration from clumpy accretion-disk winds has been invoked to explain the extreme X-ray weakness and X-ray variability observed in a substantial fraction of super-Eddington accreting quasars. We present a comprehensive study of the strong X-ray variability of the super-Eddington accreting active galactic nucleus (AGN) I Zwicky 1 (I Zw 1), a prototypical narrow-line} Seyfert 1 galaxy (NLS1), to test the disk-wind obscuration scenario as the underlying mechanism and characterizing the disk-wind absorber properties. We focus on spectral and temporal analyses of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations in 2020, and a 100-day NICER monitoring campaign in 2022. Despite strong X-ray variability by factors of $\approx3$ and $\approx6$ on short-term and long-term timescales, respectively, the XMM-Newton Optical Monitor observations do not show contemporaneous significant UV variability, and archival data reveal only mild long-term optical/infrared variability ($\approx30\%$), indicating a stable accretion process in I Zw 1. The strong X-ray variability thus likely arises from variable absorption of relatively stable coronal emission. We perform time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy utilizing a partial-covering absorption model with a stable corona and varying ionized absorbers. We identify three distinct absorbers whose variations in the column density and covering factor successfully explain the observed X-ray ``flares'' in 2020 and the longer-term spectral evolution in 2022. Our results support a unified scenario in which obscuration from clumpy disk winds produces the strong X-ray variability observed in super-Eddington accreting AGNs. This scenario may be applicable to other NLS1s exhibiting strong X-ray variability to better characterize the disk winds driven by super-Eddington accretion.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that variable absorption by clumpy accretion-disk winds explains the strong X-ray variability in the super-Eddington accreting AGN I Zw 1, supporting a unified model for disk wind-driven obscuration in such systems.
AI.motivation: To test the disk-wind obscuration scenario as the underlying mechanism behind the extreme X-ray weakness and variability observed in super-Eddington accreting quasars, specifically in the AGN I Zw 1.
AI.method: Spectral and temporal analyses of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations (2020) and a 100-day NICER monitoring campaign (2022) were performed, using time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy with a partial-covering absorption model involving a stable corona and varying ionized absorbers.
AI.result: The study identified three distinct ionized absorbers whose variations in column density and covering factor explain the observed X-ray flares and spectral evolution, supporting that clumpy disk wind obscuration causes strong X-ray variability in super-Eddington accreting AGNs.
AI.conclusion: Obscuration from clumpy accretion-disk winds is the primary driver of the strong X-ray variability seen in I Zw 1, a prototypical super-Eddington accreting AGN, and this scenario may be applicable to other narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies with similar variability.

title: Magnetic field dynamics in isolated neutron stars with an external dipole field
summary: Neutron stars can harbor extremely strong magnetic fields, yet the structure and stability of their magnetic field configuration remain poorly understood. Observations of pulsars indicate that the large-scale external field is predominantly dipolar far from the star, while the internal magnetic configurations are largely unconstrained. We investigate the dynamical stability of magnetized neutron stars through long-term numerical-relativity simulations. We explore a range of models with an initial external dipole field and mixed poloidal-toroidal internal field where the energy of the toroidal component varies up to $80\%$ of the magnetic energy. We find that the internal magnetic field relaxes toward a dynamically stable mixed poloidal-toroidal geometry, in which the toroidal component contributes to $\lesssim10\%$ of the total magnetic energy both in the exterior and in the interior. This configuration emerges within one Alfvén time following the saturation of the Tayler instabilities and also aided by gravitational-wave emission. These results suggest that long-lived neutron star magnetic fields are strongly constrained toward stable mixed configurations, with important implications for pulsar emission models, magnetar evolution, and the interpretation of gravitational-wave signals from magnetized remnants.

AI.tldr: Simulations reveal neutron star magnetic fields stabilize as mixed poloidal-toroidal structures with minimal toroidal energy (~10%), influencing astrophysical and gravitational-wave models.
AI.motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of neutron star magnetic fields, which remain poorly constrained particularly internally, is crucial for interpreting pulsar emissions, magnetar evolution, and gravitational-wave signals.
AI.method: Conducted long-term numerical-relativity simulations of neutron stars with initial external dipole and mixed poloidal-toroidal internal magnetic fields, varying the toroidal energy component up to 80%.
AI.result: Found that internal magnetic fields dynamically relax to a stable mixed poloidal-toroidal configuration with the toroidal component contributing less than about 10% of total magnetic energy, stabilized within one Alfvén time after Tayler instability saturation and aided by gravitational-wave emission.
AI.conclusion: Neutron star magnetic fields are strongly constrained toward long-lived, stable mixed poloidal-toroidal configurations with dominant dipolar external fields, impacting models of pulsar emission, magnetar evolution, and gravitational-wave interpretations.

title: \texttt{calypso}: a Parameter-Conditioned Stochastic Surrogate Model for Circumbinary Accretion Time-Series
summary: We present calypso, a parameter-conditioned stochastic surrogate model for circumbinary accretion flows. We represent the total and individual accretion time series in a PCA basis and model the resulting coefficients as draws from a multivariate Gaussian distribution over the latent PCA coefficients. We specifically include the aleatoric uncertainty of the time series in the model, enabling the emulator to capture the inherent stochasticity of the accretion process and the long-term modulation due to disk precession. We further explore the epistemic uncertainty in the model due to limited training data and interpolation in the ($e_{\rm b}$, $q_{\rm b}$) parameter space and find that the data does not support inclusion of this added variance term. We present the properties of existing simulation suites of circumbinary accretion, and run new simulations to fill in gaps in the parameter space, as well as a set of 13 test simulations for validation of the emulator. We publish calypso as a pip-installable Python package with an open-source codebase and comprehensive documentation, and demonstrate use-cases for current and upcoming transient surveys. We additionally derive a closed-form Gaussian likelihood that enables direct inference of ($e_{\rm b}$, $q_{\rm b}$) from observed accretion-rate time series.

AI.tldr: Calypso is a PCA-based stochastic surrogate model for circumbinary accretion flows, capturing inherent stochasticity and enabling parameter inference, validated by simulations and distributed as an open-source Python package.
AI.motivation: To model and predict circumbinary accretion flows with uncertainty quantification, addressing limitations in existing simulation data and capturing stochastic behavior.
AI.method: Represent accretion time series in PCA basis; model PCA coefficients as draws from a multivariate Gaussian capturing aleatoric uncertainty; investigate epistemic uncertainty due to limited training data and parameter interpolation; run additional simulations to fill parameter space gaps; validate with test simulations; provide a Python package implementing the emulator.
AI.result: Developed calypso, a stochastic surrogate model that captures both aleatoric uncertainty and long-term modulation in circumbinary accretion flows; found epistemic uncertainty addition unnecessary; published a pip-installable, open-source Python package; derived a closed-form Gaussian likelihood for direct parameter inference from observed data.
AI.conclusion: The calypso model effectively emulates circumbinary accretion flows with quantified aleatoric uncertainty and practical usability via open-source software, enabling parameter inference and supporting transient survey analyses.

title: A No-Go Theorem for the Mass-Radius Relation of Solitons
summary: We prove a no-go theorem for the mass-radius relation of localized and stable field configurations, known as solitons. Defining the mass-radius index by $Γ\equiv \frac{\rm{d}\ln M}{\rm{d}\ln R}$, for real scalar field theories in $d$ spatial dimensions, we show that typical non-topological, non-relativistic, and spherically symmetric solitons cannot have $Γ$ in the range $[0, d]$. The forces considered originate from gradient energy, self-interaction, and gravitation, with the typicality assumption excluding the fine-tuned region of the parameter space where all three forces have comparable strength. Importantly, the theorem works for an arbitrary self-interaction that, in the relativistic theory, is allowed to be non-power-law in the field, be non-analytic around the classical vacuum (where the field amplitude vanishes), or to include derivative couplings. Additionally, the theorem makes no assumptions about the explicit form of the soliton's density profile or the behavior of $Γ$ as a function of $R$. We also argue that the same exclusion applies to compact objects formed from self-gravitating, non-relativistic, barotropic fluids with arbitrary equations of state. As a consequence for cosmology, it is worth noting that observations favor a core in the centers of dark matter halos with $Γ\simeq 1.7$, which (for $d=3$) lies approximately in the middle of the excluded range. Therefore, proposals such as ultra-light or fluid-like dark matter models are essentially ruled out as natural explanations for halo cores, provided other astrophysical effects are negligible.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem that typical stable scalar field solitons cannot have mass-radius scaling indices between 0 and the number of spatial dimensions. This excludes many proposed dark matter models from naturally explaining observed dark matter halo cores with mass-radius index around 1.7 in three dimensions.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous constraints on the mass-radius scaling of stable, localized field configurations (solitons) in scalar field theories, motivated by the need to understand astrophysical and cosmological structures such as dark matter halo cores.
AI.method: Proving a no-go theorem by analyzing the mass-radius index \(Γ = \frac{d\ln M}{d\ln R}\) for real scalar fields in \(d\) spatial dimensions, under typical assumptions on forces (gradient, self-interaction, gravitation) excluding fine-tuned parameter regimes, and making no restrictive assumptions on soliton profiles or interaction forms.
AI.result: Demonstration that typical non-topological, non-relativistic, spherically symmetric solitons cannot have mass-radius index \(Γ\) within the range \([0, d]\), and that similar exclusions apply to compact self-gravitating barotropic fluid objects with arbitrary equations of state. Observations of dark matter halo cores with \(Γ \simeq 1.7\) for \(d=3\) fall inside the excluded range, ruling out certain dark matter models as natural explanations for halo cores.
AI.conclusion: The no-go theorem imposes fundamental constraints that exclude typical scalar field solitons and fluid-like models from explaining the core structure observed in dark matter halos, specifically disallowing mass-radius scalings in the range \([0, d]\), and implying the need for alternative astrophysical mechanisms or model classes.

title: The $τ$ of Neutral Hydrogen: Increased CMB Optical Depth at Long Wavelengths
summary: At wavelengths longer than 21 cm, photons from the long-wavelength tail of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) have a non-zero probability of being absorbed by distant neutral hydrogen. This provides an additional suppression of the observed CMB clustering in addition to the usual Thomson scattering. The optical depth as a function of frequency is sensitive to the 21 cm spin temperature $T_s$ of the gas as a function of cosmic time, with the excess optical depth peaking at a level of a few percent around 100 MHz. The details depend on the specifics of the heating of cosmic gas and the evolution of the neutral fraction $x_{HI}$. It is likely difficult to detect the CMB at these long radio wavelengths, but the cause is aided by the ability to cross-correlate with the already well-characterized fluctuations at cm/mm frequencies. We find that detecting CMB fluctuations at radio wavelengths corresponding to the 21 cm ``dark ages'' in cross-correlation with mm-wave maps may be easier than detecting the intrinsic 21 cm fluctuations. Measurement of the amplitude of CMB fluctuations as a function of radio wavelength provides a path for a new type of direct measurement of the combination $x_{HI}/T_s$ as a function of redshift.

AI.tldr: This study examines how neutral hydrogen absorbs CMB photons at wavelengths >21 cm, causing additional CMB clustering suppression, and suggests cross-correlating radio and mm-wave maps as a promising method to detect and measure the neutral hydrogen fraction to spin temperature ratio over redshift.
AI.motivation: To explore the detectability and implications of CMB photon absorption by neutral hydrogen at wavelengths longer than 21 cm and how this affects CMB clustering observations.
AI.method: Analysis of the optical depth of CMB photons due to 21 cm absorption, modeling its dependence on gas spin temperature and neutral fraction evolution, and proposing cross-correlation techniques with mm-wave maps to detect these effects.
AI.result: The excess optical depth due to 21 cm absorption peaks at a few percent near 100 MHz, offering an additional suppression of CMB clustering; cross-correlation with known mm-wave fluctuations may facilitate detection, providing a novel route to measure the ratio of neutral hydrogen fraction to spin temperature across redshifts.
AI.conclusion: CMB fluctuations at long radio wavelengths can be indirectly detected through cross-correlation with mm-wave data, enabling direct measurement of the combination $x_{HI}/T_s$ over cosmic time, which enriches our understanding of the neutral hydrogen evolution during the cosmic dark ages.

title: Constraining the Photon Intensity of Extragalactic Background Light with the HAWC Observatory for the Blazar Mrk 421
summary:
The blazar Mrk 421 exhibits rapid variability over a wide range of timescales. Spectral differences have been observed during the different emission states of Mrk 421. During the high emission states, tests to constraint the Hubble constant and the photon intensity of Extragalactic Background Light (EBL) can be performed. The HAWC observatory provides an exceptionally long term monitoring of the source at TeV energies. We selected periods of high emission state and low emission state in data with total observation time of 2460 transits from the HAWC observatory using the All-sky Root around in an Unbiased way methodology.
  We report on evidence of a cutoff in the spectrum of Mrk 421 during high emission states. An Exponential Cutoff Power Law is preferred over a Simple Power Law at a $3.8\,σ$ level. In the Exponential Cutoff Power Law, the cutoff is found at $13\pm3~\text{TeV}$. Using this result, we provide upper limits on the specific intensity of EBL photons. Moreover, the value of the energy cutoff found in our analysis is different from the cutoff expected by the interaction of gamma-rays with EBL photons. This result indicates that the cutoff is intrinsic to the source.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes long-term HAWC data of blazar Mrk 421, finding a significant intrinsic spectral cutoff at ~13 TeV during high emission states, which helps constrain EBL intensity and informs understanding of the source's emission physics.
AI.motivation: To study the spectral variability of the blazar Mrk 421 during different emission states and to use these observations to constrain cosmological parameters and the Extragalactic Background Light (EBL).
AI.method: Long-term monitoring data from the HAWC observatory over 2460 transits was analyzed using the All-sky Root around in an Unbiased way methodology to select high and low emission states of Mrk 421, followed by spectral analysis testing models with and without an exponential cutoff.
AI.result: Evidence of a spectral cutoff at 13±3 TeV during high emission states was found, with the Exponential Cutoff Power Law preferred over the Simple Power Law at 3.8σ significance. The cutoff differs from that expected from gamma-ray interactions with EBL photons, suggesting it is intrinsic to the source. Upper limits on the EBL photon intensity were also provided.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic spectral cutoff observed in Mrk 421 during high emission states indicates the cutoff is a source property rather than caused by gamma-ray absorption by EBL, enabling constraints on the EBL intensity and insights into the blazar's emission mechanisms.

title: Gravitational waves from cosmic strings with friction: analytical approximations and parameter space
summary: We derive analytical approximations to describe the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak of the stochastic gravitational wave background generated by cosmic strings that is sourced by loops created in the friction-dominated era. We show that these approximations provide a very good description of the contribution of the friction-era loops over the relevant frequency range and for a broad range of cosmic string parameters, thus enabling a fast and accurate characterization of this signature. We also use these approximations to uncover the full parameter range in which this ultra-high-frequency peak should be distinguishable on the stochastic gravitational wave background spectrum and show that it should be present in a broader range of high-energy physics scenarios than originally reported in~\cite{Mukovnikov:2024zed}.

AI.tldr: This paper derives accurate analytical formulas to describe the ultra-high-frequency peak in the gravitational wave background from cosmic string loops formed in the friction era, showing this peak is identifiable in a wider range of scenarios than previously known.
AI.motivation: To characterize the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak in the stochastic gravitational wave background generated by cosmic strings, particularly those from loops created in the friction-dominated era, which had not been fully explored before.
AI.method: Derivation of analytical approximations to describe the contribution of friction-era cosmic string loops to the stochastic gravitational wave background at ultra-high frequencies, validated across a broad range of parameters.
AI.result: The derived approximations provide a very accurate and fast description of the friction-era loop contributions over relevant frequencies, enabling identification of the full parameter space where the ultra-high-frequency peak is distinguishable. The study finds the peak should appear in a wider range of high-energy physics scenarios than previously reported.
AI.conclusion: Analytical approximations successfully capture the friction-era cosmic string loop contributions to the stochastic gravitational wave background, extending the expected domain for the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak beyond prior work.

title: Inferring the role of binary neutron star mergers in r-process nucleosynthesis with multi-messenger observations using Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope
summary: Identifying the cosmic origin of rapid neutron-capture (r-process) elements remains an open problem. Binary neutron-star (BNS) mergers and rare classes of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) represent the main contenders as major r-process production sites. Although BNS mergers could exclusively account for r-process nucleosynthesis, results from chemical evolution studies taking into account their delays with respect to star formation, observed BNS rates by gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, as well as issues with retention in low-mass halos suggest otherwise. Here, we propose a method to measure the contribution of BNS mergers to cosmic r-process nucleosynthesis with the third-generation GW detectors Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope. It exploits the redshift-dependent correlation between the total number of BNS GW events and the average r-process abundances at redshifts $z \lesssim 1$. We apply this correlation technique to mock GW and abundance data, accounting for expected observational uncertainties in two limiting scenarios: GW events with electromagnetic counterpart (multi-messenger 'bright-sirens') and without ('dark-sirens'). Using Fisher forecasts, we demonstrate that the fractional cumulative contribution of BNS mergers to the total cosmic r-process $F_{\rm{BNS,z0}}$ can be estimated to the $\lesssim 5-6\%$ precision level for both scenarios at $1σ$ for fiducial astrophysical scenarios with $F_{\rm{BNS,z0}} \gtrsim 0.1-1$. Furthermore, the method also yields estimates of the BNS delay-time distribution parameters comparable to other approaches. Although cosmic r-process abundances may be reconstructed from local observations at low metallicity, this method also provides a science case to identify signatures of neutron-capture elements beyond the local Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method using future gravitational-wave detectors to correlate binary neutron-star merger events with cosmic r-process element abundances, enabling precise estimation of the mergers' contribution to heavy element synthesis and the delay-time characteristics of these events.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to resolve the open problem of identifying the cosmic origin of rapid neutron-capture (r-process) elements, considering that current candidates like binary neutron-star mergers and rare core-collapse supernovae have unresolved issues in explaining observed r-process abundances.
AI.method: The paper proposes a new method that leverages redshift-dependent correlations between gravitational-wave detected binary neutron-star merger events and average r-process abundances at redshifts less than approximately 1, using future third-generation GW detectors. It applies this method to mock multi-messenger and dark-siren data with Fisher matrix forecasts to estimate key parameters.
AI.result: The method can estimate the fractional cumulative contribution of binary neutron-star mergers to total cosmic r-process production with a precision better than 5-6% at one sigma level for astrophysical scenarios where this contribution is above 10-100%. It also provides estimates for the binary neutron-star delay-time distribution parameters comparable to existing methods. Additionally, it enables studies of neutron-capture element signatures beyond the local Universe.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that the proposed redshift-dependent correlation technique using third-generation GW data offers a precise and independent means to quantify the contribution of binary neutron-star mergers to cosmic r-process nucleosynthesis, addressing limitations of current approaches and expanding the scope to extragalactic observations.

title: Increasing the Precision of Surrogate Models for Weak Lensing Mass Maps with Flow Matching
summary: Weak gravitational lensing maps compactly encode the evolution of cosmic large-scale structure and are a key tool for cosmological analyses. Performing inference directly at the map level allows flexible choices of statistics and can increase constraining power. Conventional methods rely solely on N-body simulations and are computationally expensive. Generative machine-learning emulators can accelerate map-level theory prediction. However, existing GAN-based map-level surrogates still have limited statistical fidelity. They can produce over-smoothed maps, may fail to capture the full distribution of generated map sets and can be difficult to train. Continuous normalizing flows trained with flow matching have recently emerged as a powerful class of generative models. We present a residual label-conditional flow matching generative network that conditions explicitly on the matter density Omega_m and clustering amplitude sigma_8 for a fixed source redshift distribution n(z). The model learns a continuous probability flow in a residual space from label-specific noise distributions to convergence maps. We evaluate it using pixel and peak statistics, the power spectrum, bispectrum, power-spectrum correlation matrices, and other validation metrics. Compared with the previous GAN benchmark, the proposed method improves the typical fidelity of generated maps from below 10% and below 20% to below 1% and below 5% for basic and higher-order statistics, respectively. The agreement at the level of map distributions is also very good: maps generated from random noise match well the distribution of maps generated with N-body simulations from random initial conditions. This work brings us closer to a practical mass-map emulator that captures the cosmological signal while supporting multiple forms of data analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a continuous normalizing flow-based generative model that accurately emulates weak gravitational lensing maps conditioned on cosmological parameters, outperforming GAN-based methods in fidelity and paving the way for efficient and flexible cosmological inference at the map level.
AI.motivation: To improve computational efficiency and statistical fidelity in generating weak gravitational lensing maps, a key tool for cosmological analyses, by developing a more accurate and flexible generative model than existing GAN-based surrogates.
AI.method: Develop a residual label-conditional flow matching generative network that conditions on cosmological parameters (matter density Omega_m and clustering amplitude sigma_8) to produce convergence maps, trained via continuous normalizing flows and flow matching to learn a probability flow from label-specific noise to maps.
AI.result: The proposed method significantly outperforms previous GAN-based models, reducing fidelity errors in basic and higher-order statistics to below 1% and 5%, respectively, and producing map distributions closely matching those from N-body simulations.
AI.conclusion: The residual label-conditional flow matching generative model offers a practical and statistically faithful mass-map emulator for weak gravitational lensing, enabling flexible analyses while efficiently capturing cosmological signals.

title: Dissecting the Perseus-Pisces supercluster observed with CFHT-MegaCam: Exploring late-type galaxy shape alignments within the local cosmic web
summary: Intrinsic alignments of galaxy shapes are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and provide insight into how galaxies acquire orientations within the cosmic web. Most studies rely on large statistical samples; here, we probe this signal in a single nearby superstructure, extending to outer regions where secondary infall should dominate. We measure intrinsic alignments in the Perseus-Pisces supercluster as a function of galaxy morphology and radial extent into the low surface brightness regime. Using deep CFHT r-band imaging covering 367 deg2 (mainly from the UNIONS survey) and reaching 28 mag/arcsec2, we compute correlation functions at three isophotal radii for 2004 galaxies with log M*/Msun > 8.6, stratified by morphology and stellar mass in comoving coordinates. We detect positive intrinsic alignment signals for both early- and late-type galaxies out to 1 Mpc/h, including a clear signal for spirals. Shape-shape correlations are stronger than position-shape correlations, while comoving measurements increase the fraction of strongly correlated systems. Correlation profiles show little radial dependence across the three isophotes despite ellipticity variations in 10-20% of galaxies. We find strong morphology dependence: late-type galaxies dominate the shape-shape signal, preferentially inhabiting filaments and displaying higher ellipticities consistent with edge-on orientations. Early-type galaxies instead cluster near group and cluster centers, with no comparable excess in position-shape correlations. This segregation suggests distinct alignment mechanisms: tidal stretching for early-types in dense environments and tidal torquing for late-types in filaments. These local-Universe constraints inform intrinsic alignment modeling for Euclid, DESI, and LSST, highlighting the contribution of blue spiral galaxies to low-redshift cosmic shear contamination.

AI.tldr: This study probes intrinsic galaxy shape alignments in the Perseus-Pisces supercluster, revealing morphology-dependent correlations driven by different tidal mechanisms, crucial for modeling systematics in upcoming weak lensing surveys.
AI.motivation: To investigate intrinsic alignments of galaxy shapes within a single nearby superstructure, extending to outer regions dominated by secondary infall, to better understand galaxy orientation mechanisms and improve weak lensing systematic modeling.
AI.method: Measured intrinsic alignments in the Perseus-Pisces supercluster using deep CFHT r-band imaging covering 367 deg2, reaching 28 mag/arcsec2. Computed correlation functions for 2004 galaxies stratified by morphology and stellar mass at three isophotal radii in comoving coordinates.
AI.result: Detected positive intrinsic alignment signals for both early- and late-type galaxies out to 1 Mpc/h, with stronger shape-shape than position-shape correlations. Late-type galaxies dominate shape-shape signals, inhabiting filaments with higher ellipticities; early-types cluster near group centers with distinct alignment mechanisms. Correlation profiles show little radial dependence across isophotes.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic alignments vary strongly with morphology, driven by tidal torquing in late-type galaxies within filaments and tidal stretching in early-types in dense environments. These findings constrain intrinsic alignment models for future cosmological surveys and highlight the contamination from blue spiral galaxies in low-redshift cosmic shear analyses.

title: Hydrodynamic model of nonthermal emission from the Fermi bubbles
comment: 26 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to Astroparticle Physics
summary:
We suggest a model of Fermi Bubbles (FBs) in the Galactic halo of the altitude about 7-8 kpc, which is seen in non-thermal microwave and gamma-ray ranges. It was assumed that this emission is generated by relativistic electrons of cosmic rays whose origin is still under debate. It has been assumed that the FB shell is generated in the halo by the release of energy, generated by the routine capture of stars at the central black hole of the Galactic Centre (GC). In this case cosmic ray electrons (CR) in the shells of the FBs of sufficiently high energies are generated by the standard shock acceleration. However, one of the problems of this model is that the Mach number of the FB shock is not high enough to generate the observed non-thermal radiation from the halo.
  We propose an alternative model of stochastic CR acceleration by Rayleigh-Taylor (RT) instabilities in the shell of the FB at the late stages of the evolution of the shell in the halo. Unlike the shock model of CR acceleration, the RT model of in-situ acceleration in the FBs does not require strong shock fronts. In our model, we derived the spectrum of RT instabilities and estimate the spectra of kinetic equations for MHD-fluctuations needed for acceleration of CRs. We assessed the time of CR electron acceleration up to TeV energies that needed to interpret the observed data of gamma-ray and microwave emission from the envelope of FBs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities in the Fermi Bubble shells stochastically accelerate cosmic ray electrons to TeV energies, explaining observed non-thermal emissions without relying on strong shock fronts, which are insufficient in standard models.
AI.motivation: The origin and acceleration mechanism of relativistic cosmic ray electrons responsible for the non-thermal microwave and gamma-ray emission of the Fermi Bubbles in the Galactic halo remain unclear, especially given that shock acceleration models struggle due to insufficient Mach numbers of the shocks.
AI.method: They propose a model of stochastic cosmic ray acceleration driven by Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities within the FB shell, deriving the instability spectrum and solving kinetic equations for MHD fluctuations to estimate electron acceleration times to TeV energies, contrasting this with the standard shock acceleration approach.
AI.result: Their model suggests that Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities can efficiently accelerate cosmic ray electrons in situ within the Fermi Bubble shells without requiring strong shock fronts, providing a viable explanation for the observed gamma-ray and microwave emissions.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic acceleration of cosmic ray electrons via Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities in the FB shells is a plausible and effective mechanism to generate the observed high-energy non-thermal emission, overcoming limitations of traditional shock acceleration models.

title: Cosmological constraints from neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions
summary: We investigate whether neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions (MCFs) can extract cosmological information beyond the standard redshift-space two-point correlation function (2PCF). Using the Kun suite of 129 $w_0w_a$CDM$+\sum m_ν$ simulations in $1~h^{-1}{\rm Gpc}$ boxes, we construct Gaussian-process emulators for the normalized scale statistic $\widehat{W}^α(s)$ and the angular statistic $\widehat{W}^α_{Δs}(μ)$. We perform joint analyses combining multiple mark parameters $α$ and quantify the information gain using the FoM in the $Ω_m$--$σ_8$ plane. Relative to the 2PCF case, three-mark combinations improve the FoM by factors of $1.7$--$2.5$, while five-mark combinations increase the gain to $1.9$--$2.4$, depending on the statistic and mark definition. We further compare density and normalized-gradient marks, finding that they are nearly redundant for isotropic statistics but complementary for angular statistics, where their combination improves the FoM by up to $43\%$. Tests of scale range and halo selection show that the marked statistics remain robust under changes in analysis choices, with the angular statistic retaining additional cosmological information that is less sensitive to tracer selection. Our results demonstrate that MCFs substantially enhance cosmological constraints beyond the standard 2PCF and provide a robust probe for next-generation galaxy surveys.

AI.tldr: The study shows that neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions improve cosmological constraints beyond standard two-point statistics, with gains validated across simulations and robust under analysis variations, offering a powerful tool for upcoming galaxy surveys.
AI.motivation: To evaluate if neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions can provide additional cosmological information beyond the conventional redshift-space two-point correlation function.
AI.method: Utilized the Kun simulation suite of 129 cosmological models to build Gaussian-process emulators for normalized scale and angular marked correlation statistics, performing joint parameter analyses and information quantification using the Figure of Merit (FoM) in the Ω_m–σ_8 parameter space.
AI.result: Three-mark combinations improved the FoM by 1.7–2.5 times and five-mark combinations by 1.9–2.4 times relative to the standard 2PCF; density and normalized-gradient marks showed complementary behavior in angular statistics, boosting FoM by up to 43%. The marked statistics remained robust across varied scale ranges and halo selections, particularly the angular statistics exhibiting less sensitivity to tracer selection.
AI.conclusion: Marked correlation functions significantly enhance cosmological parameter constraints compared to the standard two-point correlation function and provide a robust method for analysis in future galaxy surveys.

title: An extremely bright slow-rising afterglow from an off-axis jet in GRB 260310A
summary: We present a multi-wavelength study of GRB 260310A, a nearby long-duration gamma-ray burst at $z\simeq0.153$ associated with a broad-lined Type Ic supernova. Despite its modest prompt gamma-ray output, $E_{γ,\rm iso}\simeq3.5\times10^{50}$ erg, GRB\,260310A exhibits one of the brightest afterglows ever observed in the X-ray, optical, and radio bands. Its apparent brightness is not its only remarkable feature. The optical afterglow displays a delayed onset, characterized by a slow rising phase, with slope $α\approx-1$, and a late peak at $\approx$0.1 d. We argue that the combination of weak prompt emission, hard peak energy, and late afterglow onset is naturally explained by a GRB jet viewed off-axis. The radio spectral energy distributions are consistent with synchrotron radiation and indicate the presence of both reverse- and forward-shock components, thus providing a first test of reverse-shock models in an off-axis geometry. The X-ray afterglow displays a prominent rebrightening, monitored for up to $\approx$68 d with no evidence of spectral evolution. A low level of linear polarization, $Π\approx1.7\%$, is measured at 15 GHz at $T_0+55$ d and suggests that, at these late times, the forward-shock is the dominant emission component from radio to X-rays. This late-time rebrightening represents a critical test for the two-component jet model. If interpreted as the emergence of a narrow jet core viewed further off-axis, it would imply extreme luminosities and energetics for an on-axis observer.

AI.tldr: GRB 260310A features an unusually bright afterglow with delayed onset explained by an off-axis jet; radio and X-ray data reveal complex shock dynamics and late rebrightening consistent with a two-component jet model.
AI.motivation: To investigate the unique properties of GRB 260310A, a nearby long-duration gamma-ray burst with atypical afterglow features.
AI.method: A multi-wavelength observational study including X-ray, optical, and radio data was conducted, analyzing spectral energy distributions and polarization measurements.
AI.result: GRB 260310A shows an exceptionally bright afterglow despite weak prompt emission, explained by an off-axis jet viewing angle. Radio data confirm the presence of reverse- and forward-shock components. The X-ray afterglow exhibits late-time rebrightening without spectral changes, and low radio polarization suggests forward-shock dominance. The late rebrightening supports a two-component jet model but implies extreme energetics if viewed on-axis.
AI.conclusion: The observations of GRB 260310A strongly support an off-axis jet scenario with combined reverse- and forward-shock contributions, challenging standard interpretations of energetics and jet structure in gamma-ray bursts.

title: Scalable Dark Siren Cosmology with gwcosmo: GPU Acceleration, Validation and Systematics
summary: As the number of confident gravitational-wave detections grows, population-level hierarchical analyses face increasing computational costs. Dark-siren cosmological inference integrates over the localisation volume of each gravitational-wave source. To remain feasible without discarding information from the quieter but more numerous sources in the catalogue, significant efficiency improvements are vital for analysis pipelines. In this work, we present an upgraded version of the cosmological inference pipeline gwcosmo, which leverages vectorisation on graphics processing units to process the entire gravitational-wave catalogue in parallel with each iteration. This new implementation achieves a speed-up of 1000 times over the previous version, facilitating analyses of O5-like numbers of GW events on wall-clock timescales of hours. Our results demonstrate the scalability of the gwcosmo pipeline, specifically its ability to handle the increasing computational load of expanding event catalogues, positioning it as a vital tool for future advances in dark-siren cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an upgraded gwcosmo pipeline using GPU vectorisation to speed up dark-siren cosmological inference by 1000x, enabling scalable analysis of large gravitational-wave event catalogues in hours.
AI.motivation: Increasing number of gravitational-wave detections leads to higher computational costs for population-level hierarchical analyses, necessitating efficiency improvements for cosmological inference pipelines, especially to include numerous quiet sources without discarding data.
AI.method: Upgraded the cosmological inference pipeline gwcosmo by leveraging vectorisation on graphics processing units (GPUs) to process the entire gravitational-wave catalogue in parallel during each iteration.
AI.result: Achieved a speed-up of 1000 times compared to the previous version, enabling analysis of O5-like numbers of gravitational-wave events within hours and demonstrating the pipeline's scalability to handle expanding event catalogues.
AI.conclusion: The upgraded gwcosmo pipeline, with GPU vectorisation and parallel processing, substantially increases computational efficiency and scalability, making it a crucial tool for future dark-siren cosmology studies involving large gravitational-wave datasets.

title: Minor Merger, Major Growth: An Overmassive, Highly Accreting Black Hole Powering a Secondary AGN In a Cosmic Noon Minor Merger
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We report the discovery of a spectroscopically confirmed z = 1.824 minor merger with a mass ratio of ~35:1 in which the secondary (smaller) galaxy hosts a luminous AGN. The system is identified in the 3D-HST survey and exhibits clear tidal features in James Webb Space Telescope imaging, confirming an ongoing interaction. Using archival Chandra X-ray observations, we detect 121 +/- 11 X-ray counts associated with the secondary galaxy, corresponding to a rest-frame 2-10 keV luminosity of L_X ~ (9 +/- 0.1) x 10^43 erg/s and a photon index of Gamma ~ 2.0-2.3. Analysis of the HST/WFC3 G141 grism spectrum yields an [O III] lambda5007 luminosity of (2 +/- 0.5) x 10^42 erg/s. Independent bolometric luminosity estimates from X-ray and [O III] emission are consistent, implying L_bol ~ (3-7) x 10^45 erg/s. Assuming standard black hole-galaxy scaling relations, the expected black hole mass is ~2 x 10^6 M_sun, which would require extreme super-Eddington accretion to explain the observed luminosity. On the other hand, assuming Eddington-limited or moderately sub-Eddington accretion implies a black hole mass more than an order of magnitude above expectations. The observed X-ray spectral slope disfavors low accretion rates, restricting the allowed parameter space to high lambda_Edd and elevated black hole masses. We conclude that the secondary AGN must be powered by an overmassive, highly accreting black hole, providing direct observational support for theoretical predictions that minor mergers can drive rapid black hole growth in secondary, smaller companions.

AI.tldr: A z=1.824 minor merger featuring a luminous AGN in the smaller galaxy shows evidence of an overmassive, rapidly accreting black hole, supporting the theory that minor mergers promote fast black hole growth in secondary companions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature of a minor merger system with a luminous AGN in the smaller galaxy and understand black hole accretion processes in such mergers.
AI.method: Identification of the system in the 3D-HST survey, analysis of JWST imaging for tidal features, use of archival Chandra X-ray data to measure X-ray counts and luminosity, spectroscopic analysis of HST/WFC3 G141 grism data for [O III] emission, and comparison of bolometric luminosities with black hole-galaxy scaling relations and accretion models.
AI.result: The secondary galaxy hosts a luminous AGN with X-ray and [O III] luminosities consistent with a bolometric luminosity of (3-7) x 10^45 erg/s. Standard scaling relations suggest the black hole mass is ~2 x 10^6 M_sun, but this would require super-Eddington accretion rates, which is disfavored by the X-ray spectral slope. Instead, the data implies an overmassive black hole with high accretion rates, supporting rapid black hole growth driven by minor mergers.
AI.conclusion: Minor mergers can drive rapid black hole growth in the smaller companion galaxies, as evidenced by the discovery of an overmassive, highly accreting black hole powering the luminous AGN in the secondary galaxy in a z=1.824 minor merger system.

title: cloelib: A Flexible Python Library for Computing Cosmological Observables in the Euclid Era
summary: cloelib is a Python library developed to compute cosmological observables within the Cosmology Likelihood for Observables in Euclid (CLOE) ecosystem (cloe-org). As cosmology enters a precision era driven by galaxy survey missions such as Euclid, there is a growing need for flexible, efficient, and differentiable software capable of supporting next-generation inference pipelines. cloelib addresses these demands through a modular architecture that interfaces seamlessly with established Boltzmann solvers whilst incorporating JAX-based automatic differentiation to enable gradient-based methods. The library defines consistent protocols for background evolution, perturbations, and non-linear structure formation, and supports a wide range of observables, including photometric and spectroscopic large-scale structure probes, as well as cross-correlations with the Cosmic Microwave Background and galaxy clusters. In its finalised form, cloelib is intended to serve as the reference theory computation infrastructure for Euclid's first cosmological release, bridging traditional numerical cosmology with modern optimisation techniques and emerging machine learning approaches to inference.

AI.tldr: cloelib is a Python library designed for precision cosmology, combining modular design, automatic differentiation via JAX, and broad observable support, aimed to underpin Euclid mission's cosmological analyses.
AI.motivation: The need for flexible, efficient, and differentiable software to support next-generation cosmological inference pipelines driven by precision galaxy survey missions like Euclid.
AI.method: Development of cloelib, a Python library with a modular architecture interfacing with Boltzmann solvers, incorporating JAX-based automatic differentiation, and defining protocols for background evolution, perturbations, and non-linear structure formation.
AI.result: cloelib supports a wide range of cosmological observables, including photometric and spectroscopic probes, cross-correlations with CMB and galaxy clusters, and is positioned as the reference theory computation infrastructure for Euclid's first cosmological release.
AI.conclusion: cloelib successfully bridges traditional numerical cosmology with modern optimisation and machine learning methods, enabling precise and flexible cosmological observable computations within the CLOE ecosystem.

title: cloelike: A Python Library for Cosmological Likelihood Inference in the Euclid Era
summary: cloelike is a Python package providing modular, composable Gaussian likelihood classes for the main cosmological large-scale structure observables targeted by the ESA Euclid space mission. It is a core component of the CLOE (Cosmology Likelihood for Observables in Euclid) ecosystem and interfaces directly with cloelib for theoretical predictions and euclidlib for reading official Euclid data products. The package implements Gaussian likelihoods covering harmonic angular power spectra and real-space two-point correlation functions for weak lensing (WL), photometric galaxy clustering (GCph), and Galaxy-Galaxy Lensing (GGL) in all joint probe combinations (3x2pt, 2x2pt), as well as spectroscopic full-shape power spectrum multipoles, and baryonic Acoustic oscillations (BAO). cloelike is actively used in internal Euclid Consortium analyses and is openly released to support community validation and reproducibility.

AI.tldr: cloelike is a Python package offering modular Gaussian likelihood tools for the Euclid mission's cosmological data, supporting key observables and joint analyses, enabling community use and validation.
AI.motivation: The need for a standardized, modular, and interoperable likelihood tool to analyze key cosmological observables targeted by the Euclid mission, enhancing reproducibility and community validation.
AI.method: The package implements modular and composable Gaussian likelihood classes for various large-scale structure observables, interfacing with theoretical prediction and data reading libraries to handle angular power spectra, two-point correlation functions, and power spectrum multipoles in multiple probe combinations.
AI.result: cloelike is actively used within the Euclid Consortium for data analysis and is publicly available, facilitating consistent and reproducible cosmological inference across multiple probes and data types.
AI.conclusion: cloelike provides a robust and flexible framework for cosmological likelihood analysis, crucial for the ESA Euclid mission and the broader research community.
